question: Can the catalogue reach 80% field fill with the current schemas?
answer: No. Best case at every measured source ceiling is 49.3%.
why: Overall fill is filled/declared slots. Grocery is 64.4% of all declared slots (1,026,255 of 1,594,100), so overall fill is dominated by grocery's fill. Non-grocery slots total 567,845 — even at a perfect 100% they supply only 45% of what 80% requires. Grocery must therefore reach 69% of its own slots for 80% overall, and its measured ceiling from the Blinkit pack label is 45%.

grocery.method: mean label coverage over 42 schema fields on a 1,200-page sample; verified twice independently at 45.0% and 42.6%

beauty.method: 26% of records are the Open Beauty Facts island with no GTIN bridge and no storefront

funds.method: factsheets reach 37% of records; SEBI SIDs lift sid_* and the SIP terms

phones.method: only 87 of 430 records have a reachable page; 167 are JS-rendered

crawl_vs_ceiling.note: Finishing the crawl helps, but does not close the gap.

trimming_the_sheet.note: Keeping only the best-covered grocery fields does not reach 80% either, because even the top 8 average 66.4%.

proven_absent.beauty_evidence: pao_months on 0 of 1,200 pages; Shelf Life is a different fact
proven_absent.funds_evidence: CAMS serves a byte-identical Angular shell on every serviced-AMC path; KFintech times out; AMFI publishes no mapping

what_would_change_the_answer: Pack-photo OCR for grocery — the nutrition panel and ingredient list are printed on the pack image, which Blinkit serves. This is the only route to the fields the structured data omits.
Redefining the metric to exclude fields proven absent from every reachable source, so the number measures what is obtainable rather than what was hoped for.
Accepting ~50% as the honest ceiling and reporting it as such.

pack_photo_ocr_tested.verdict: Rejected. It would address about 2% of the gap it was proposed to fix.
pack_photo_ocr_tested.why: The proposal assumed the nutrition panel is printed on a pack image Blinkit serves. It is not, for the pages that need it. 224 of the 229 food pages missing a nutrition panel carry NO full-resolution image; the 5 that do carry exactly one, which is the front of the pack, not the back where the panel is printed. Pages generally offer only CDN-resized thumbnails at 120x120 and 480x480, at which a nutrition panel is a few pixels tall and unreadable. Original assets are 1000x1000 and would be readable, but they are absent precisely where they would be needed.
pack_photo_ocr_tested.cost_avoided: The repo is stdlib-first with no requirements file. OCR would have added its first Python dependency plus a system binary in CI, for a 2% return.
pack_photo_ocr_tested.conclusion: No remaining source moves grocery past its ~45% pack-label ceiling, so 49.3% stands as the measured best case. The honest options are to accept it, or to redefine the metric so it counts only fields some reachable source actually publishes.

browser_path_tested.verdict: Works, but worth about +0.21% — not a route to 80%.
browser_path_tested.finding: The Chrome extension became available later in the session, so the 359 records recorded as needing a human page-save were re-tested. Samsung's spec page renders fully in a browser: 4000 mAh battery, 8 GB RAM, 50+10+12 MP, OIS, 120 Hz, 147.0 x 70.6 x 7.6 mm, 167 g, launch date, eSIM, Bluetooth 5.3 — about 30 fields, including year/launch_month/camera_ois/esim that an earlier pass concluded no maker publishes. They are published; they were behind JavaScript.
browser_path_tested.why_it_is_small: Discovery, not rendering, is the blocker. Samsung's sitemap has 7 entries and no per-product spec URLs, so each product needs its URL resolved by hand. Only 115 of 324 browser-blocked records (35%) carry an extractable model code. 115 records x ~30 fields = 3,450 values = +0.21% of overall fill.
browser_path_tested.also_found: Most 'phone' records for these brands are laptops — Samsung's 40 are Galaxy Books, and HP/Lenovo/Acer likewise. They are marketplace listings with model codes embedded in the title, not clean model names.

crawl_projection_corrected.finishing_existing_records: 9,208 uncrawled records lifted to the crawled rate = 102,732 values = 40.9% overall
crawl_projection_corrected.full_inventory: 57,562 pages remain of a 90,628 inventory. At the observed 87% distinct rate that is ~50,078 NEW records — but each arrives with ~38 empty slots as well as ~15.1 facts, so the full crawl lands at 37.4%, not higher. An earlier estimate of +46% counted the facts and not the slots they bring with them.
crawl_projection_corrected.conclusion: 37.4% is the projected end state of all crawling now in flight.

what_separates_a_full_record_from_an_emp.measured: 120 high-fill (>=70%) pages against 859 low-fill (<=30%) pages, same corpus

the_difference_is_the_nutrition_panel.FSSAI License: 100% vs 87% — present on both, so not the discriminator

what_separates_a_full_record_from_an_emp.so: A low-fill record is not a parsing failure. The page carries the identity fields and lacks the nutrition panel, and no amount of parser work creates one.
what_separates_a_full_record_from_an_emp.how_many_have_one: 73% of products Blinkit declares as food (veg/non-veg/egg) carry a nutrition panel. Of 2,000 sampled pages, 765 were declared non_food — soaps and cleaning supplies, where a nutrition panel correctly does not exist.
what_separates_a_full_record_from_an_emp.scale: Nutrition-derived fields account for 543,933 slots, 33% of the entire repo. All of them sit on genuinely food categories, so the sheet is not misapplied — the 27% of food packs that decline to print a panel are simply unreachable.
what_separates_a_full_record_from_an_emp.per_record_ceiling_is_NOT_the_problem: 332 grocery records already reach 80% or better and the best reaches 84% (32 of 38 fields, Kellogg's Corn Flakes). 80% per record is achievable where the pack carries a full panel. It is the 27% without one, plus the non-food products, that hold the average down.

redefining_the_metric_tested.verdict: Neither redefinition reaches 80%. The gap is not an accounting artifact — it is 543,933 nutrition slots against packs that do not all carry a panel.

prose_nutrition_reader_measured.what_it_found: A complete mandated panel written as text in a `Nutrition Information` field rather than split into structured attributes. Nothing was reading it. This disproved my earlier claim that packs without structured attributes simply do not declare nutrition.
prose_nutrition_reader_measured.correction: I described this as potentially invalidating the 45% grocery ceiling, on a 19.3% figure taken from a smaller and differently-filtered sample. The corpus-wide number is 2.2%. The ceiling analysis stands: 23.9% of food packs carry no panel in any form, structured or prose.
prose_nutrition_reader_measured.what_did_not_transfer: The same technique applied to beauty yields almost nothing. Description and Key Features are unread on 80.7% and 64.7% of pages, but the facts in them are marketing claims rather than declarations — dermatologist_tested appears in 2.8%, vegan 2.2%, pH 0.3%. `Nutrition Information` worked because it is a labelled panel; a claim in a description is not the same kind of statement.

checked_at_the_end.nova_group_looks_like_a_regression_and_i: 0% on Blinkit-crawled records against 44.8% on the older Open Food Facts import. The parser is right: the schema says NOVA is 'derived from the ingredient list by a defined method, not our judgement, and is recorded with its source'. OFF publishes it; a Blinkit page does not. All 4,450 values trace to openfoodfacts.org. Computing it ourselves would be our judgement with no source to cite.
checked_at_the_end.12,326_grocery_records_have_no_blinkit_p: They are the Open Food Facts import and were never in Blinkit's inventory, so a complete crawl could not reach them. Only 178 share an exact normalised brand+name with a Blinkit record and NONE carries a GTIN, so there is no bridge — the same island as the 862 Open Beauty Facts records.
checked_at_the_end.the_low_fields_are_dilution_not_ceiling_: energy_kcal_100g is 63.3% on crawled records against 17.0% on uncrawled, and sugars_100g 57.6% against 15.7%. Both sit below 57% overall only because the uncrawled island drags them down.

browser_path_costed.works: Samsung renders fully at the SKU URL, e.g. /galaxy-a36-5g-awesome-lavender-128gb-sm-a366elvjins/
browser_path_costed.worth: 36 Samsung + 33 Motorola + 16 OnePlus + 12 Apple + 9 Nothing = 106 records, ~3,180 values, +0.10% overall, at roughly 4 browser calls each
browser_path_costed.why_so_small: phones is 25,068 of 3,041,841 slots — 0.8% of the repo, against grocery's 64%

largest_remaining_gaps_tested.why: `npm run gaps` ranks the biggest missing-field counts in the repo. Each of the three largest was tested against the live source before being treated as a ceiling, because a large gap that is merely a parsing miss is the cheapest fill there is.

funds.plan / funds.option.verdict: ceiling — AMFI itself leaves the column blank
funds.plan / funds.option.evidence: Re-fetched NAVAll.txt through lib/polite.py: 14,340 data rows, 5,756 with a blank Plan column and 5,762 with a blank Option column. Recovery from the scheme name was tested and fails: the name carries a plan word in 8 of 5,756 rows and an option word in 42 of 5,762.
funds.plan / funds.option.why_not_guessed: Plan (Direct vs Regular) sets the expense ratio and Option (Growth vs IDCW) changes what the investor receives. Defaulting either would invent a distinction that decides returns.

grocery.quantity.verdict: ceiling — these are Open Food Facts records with no size in the name
grocery.quantity.evidence: A unit regex over the name matches 168 of 5,271 (3%).

beauty.size.evidence: A unit regex over the name matches 65 of 2,959 (2%), and several of those are 'Pack of 2' titles where the printed size is per unit, so reading the number as the pack size would be wrong.

printers_and_networking.evidence: 195 records of 99,526; filling both to 100% moves the overall figure by about 0.1 point.

beauty_open_beauty_facts_category.fill: 15.9% against a beauty domain average of 43.6%
beauty_open_beauty_facts_category.verdict: ceiling — crowd-sourced entries that cannot be matched to a crawlable page
beauty_open_beauty_facts_category.evidence: Normalised brand+name matching against the 16,579 non-OBF beauty records finds 14 matches out of 862. The records themselves show why: brands are misspelled ('Listerene', 'Loreal') and names are fragments ('boom', 'Shower Grl'), so there is no reliable key to match them to a Blinkit page or a brand storefront.
beauty_open_beauty_facts_category.why_not_fuzzy_matched: A fuzzy match would attach one product's pack facts to a different product. The 82 insurance records already carrying a name belonging to another product show what that costs.

grocery_derived_fields_rechecked.why: additives (13.9%), nova_group (6.3%) and fortified (0.4%) look like derivable fields rather than absent ones, so I retested whether they could be computed from data already held.
grocery_derived_fields_rechecked.ingredients_order_is_a_boolean: It is a flag meaning 'ingredients are listed in declared order', not the ingredient text. There is no ingredient string stored in the records to mine — a mistake worth recording, since the name reads like it holds the list.
grocery_derived_fields_rechecked.cached_pages_still_present: All 90,621 Blinkit pages remain on disk (3.5 GB at oc-crawlers/sources/blinkit/data/pages), so re-derivation needs no new crawl.
grocery_derived_fields_rechecked.additives_verdict: ceiling by deliberate design. In a 40-page sample, 23 carry ingredient text and ZERO contain an INS number — Indian labels here name additives in words. parse_pack_label.py refuses to map a name to a number (its own comment: doing so 'would put invented E-numbers on thousands of records'), and only records numbers the label prints. That restraint is correct: INS 330 is exactly citric acid, but a bare 'stabiliser' is not identifiable.
grocery_derived_fields_rechecked.nova_group_note: NOVA is computed from the ingredient list by a defined method. With no ingredient text in the records and additives unidentifiable by name, the input for that method is not held either.

headline_figure_corrected.why: The 41.80% figure excluded 3,153 grocery records whose category ('Other' 2,942, 'Confectionery' 211) is not declared in schemas/grocery.json. They are not unscored: validate.ts:111 falls back to categories._default, which declares a spec list, so the validator does hold them to it. Counting them adds 72,939 slots and 5,996 filled values, moving the headline from 41.80% to 41.02%.
headline_figure_corrected.method: Slots = sum over records of len(categories[record.category].spec), falling back to categories._default exactly as validate.ts does. Filled = attributes with a value that is not null, '', [] or {}.

sources_retested_after_challenge.why: Two populations had been called ceilings by inference rather than by test. Both were retested against live sources. One inference was wrong.

off_records_were_NOT_unreachable.claim_that_was_wrong: the 12,326 Open Food Facts grocery records have no crawlable page
off_records_were_NOT_unreachable.what_is_true: 12,116 of them carry a GTIN and 10,254 carry India's GS1 prefix (890), but only 766 have any country_of_origin recorded. fetch_dump.py lines 103-105 keep a dump row only when countries_tags contains 'india', so roughly 9,500 of our own records -- Indian barcode, blank country tag -- were very likely never matched against the dump. That is a filter too narrow, not an absent source.
off_records_were_NOT_unreachable.size: 336,969 empty slots = 10.8% of every slot in the repo, filling at 13.0%
off_records_were_NOT_unreachable.action: re-scan dispatched, keyed on the barcodes we already hold

RESULT_2026_09_06.verdict: MY HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG. This is a measured ceiling, not a filter bug.
RESULT_2026_09_06.match_rate: All 12,326 records already matched a row in the EXISTING India-filtered dump. The countries filter had excluded none of them, so widening it would have caught zero additional rows. Tested by re-running the join locally before downloading anything.
RESULT_2026_09_06.why_the_fields_are_empty: They are empty AT THE SOURCE. Dump coverage across these exact rows tracks our own fill almost exactly: energy-kcal 13.4% (we had 15%), proteins 13.3% (15%), sodium 12.0% (13%), fiber 7.0% (8%).
RESULT_2026_09_06.yield: 67 values across 40 records, not the tens of thousands I projected.
RESULT_2026_09_06.real_bug_found_anyway: The eight core panel columns were being parsed from the dump and then discarded by enrich_from_dump.py's MAP. Fixed; it will pay off whenever the dump itself improves.
RESULT_2026_09_06.corrections_to_my_figures: cohort fill is 14.1% not 13.0%; empty slots 270,562 not 336,969; country_of_origin is set on 921 not 766.

audit_catches.sodium_mg_in_a_gram_column: 2.2% of dump rows (35 of 1,616) type milligrams into the grams column — values like 1920 and 652.6 per 100 g. The median salt/sodium ratio across the dump is exactly 2.5000, confirming grams is the intended unit. Dropped as out of range, never rescaled: a contributor typo is not a unit.
audit_catches.packaging_en_placeholder: 305 of 677 candidate values are a bare 'plastic' — the same dominant-value pattern as Blinkit's '1 g'. It names a material with no form, and the enum needs both. The tail is dates, brand and city names. Only 31 of 677 were safely mappable.
audit_catches.no_nutrition_data: 84 rows declare no panel; guarded so no nutrient is written for them.

RESULT_2026_09_06.bottom_line: Open Food Facts is exhausted for these 12,326 products at ~14%. The remaining 270,498 empty slots are not reachable from this source. Filling them needs a source that actually publishes Indian panel data.

sources_retested_after_challenge.off_api_is_disallowed: world.openfoodfacts.org and in.openfoodfacts.org disallow /api/ in robots.txt; lib/polite.py refuses it. The ODbL bulk dump is the sanctioned path and is what this repo uses.

nova_group_is_derivable_and_testable.gap: missing on 47,506 grocery records; 23,524 of those carry a parsed ingredients array
nova_group_is_derivable_and_testable.sanction: the schema's own note says NOVA is derived from the ingredient list by a defined method
nova_group_is_derivable_and_testable.validation_set: 4,107 records carry BOTH an OFF-assigned NOVA group and an ingredients array, so a derivation can be measured rather than trusted. A crude 3-rule heuristic reaches 81% against them -- promising, and far too inaccurate to publish.
nova_group_is_derivable_and_testable.action: dispatched with a held-out set and a per-group precision/recall bar

medicines_blocked_by_schema_not_by_sourc.what_the_pages_hold: A survey of all 10,658 cached Health & supplements pages found regulated medicine data the repo captures none of: Salt_composition (43%, 2,822 distinct actives with strengths), Schedule H/H1/G (50%), Prescription required (58%), Medicine Type (56%), Uses_Enum (33%), Prescriber Level (51%).
medicines_blocked_by_schema_not_by_sourc.blocker: TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS in src/validate.ts is a closed allowlist (E2) and no existing grocery field can hold an active pharmaceutical ingredient or a drug schedule. CDSCO (cdsco.gov.in) is reachable and publishes drug data, but fetching it now would produce facts with nowhere to put them.
medicines_blocked_by_schema_not_by_sourc.verdict: a schema decision gates roughly 30,000 real facts already sitting on disk

sources_retested_after_challenge.serving_size_is_a_hard_ceiling: Of 32,358 cached pages for food records missing serving_size, exactly ONE states a Standard Serve Size -- and it is the '1 g' placeholder. The parser already took every real one.

alternative_indian_retailers_tested.why: The Open Food Facts result says the remaining ~270,500 empty slots need a source that publishes Indian nutrition panels. These are the candidates, tested through lib/polite.py.

bigbasket.evidence: Disallow: /p/ and Disallow: /product/ — the product pages themselves. Same position as Swiggy Instamart.

jiomart.verdict: permitted but DOES NOT PUBLISH THE PANEL
jiomart.robots: User-agent: * / Allow: / — an explicit invitation, and the sitemap works.
jiomart.evidence: Fetched a product page (Aashirvaad Multigrain Atta 5 kg, 6.8 MB). Energy 0 occurrences, FSSAI 0, Country of Origin 0, Shelf Life 0. The 'nutrition' and 'protein' hits are marketing prose, which this repo does not read as fact. Its sitemap is also only 904 curated URLs, not a catalogue.
jiomart.note: Permissive robots is not the same as having the data.

zepto.robots: User-agent: * / Allow: / — permissive, which is why an earlier note called it usable.
zepto.evidence: The homepage returns ZERO bytes to a non-browser client and both /sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml are empty. It is a JS-only app. The earlier 'usable' verdict was based on robots.txt alone and never tested against a fetch.

alternative_indian_retailers_tested.conclusion: Blinkit remains the only Indian retailer found that both permits crawling and publishes the FSS-mandated pack label as structured page data. That is why grocery's ceiling is what it is.

indian_food_brand_sites_tested.why: Brand-owned sites work for beauty (966 of 1,023 `actives` values came from brand storefronts), so the same was tested for the food brands with the most low-fill records.
indian_food_brand_sites_tested.britannia: Open robots (22 bytes, no disallows) but NO PRODUCT CATALOGUE. The site is a Next.js corporate/campaign site: its only internal links are /campaign/*, /news-and-media and policy pages. The 9 'Energy' matches I first counted were a news headline about an unrelated energy drink — a false positive from keyword counting, not a nutrition panel.
indian_food_brand_sites_tested.amul: Open robots, but zero occurrences of Nutrition, Energy, Protein, Ingredient or FSSAI on the site root.
indian_food_brand_sites_tested.parle_and_mondelez: Robots permit product paths; not pursued after the Britannia and Amul results.
indian_food_brand_sites_tested.verdict: Indian FMCG food brands publish campaign sites, not spec sheets. This is the opposite of the beauty D2C brands, which publish product catalogues via Shopify. The asymmetry is why beauty has a brand-store source kind and grocery does not.

source_hunt_summary_2026_09_06.question: Is there a legal, crawlable source for the ~270,500 empty grocery panel slots?

tested_today.Open Food Facts bulk dump: exhausted at ~14% — the data is empty at the source, not filtered out
tested_today.JioMart: robots permits everything, but publishes no panel — no Energy, FSSAI, origin or shelf life on a product page
tested_today.Zepto: robots permits everything, but serves 0 bytes to a non-browser client and has empty sitemaps
tested_today.data.gov.in: robots disallows, including its own robots.txt path
tested_today.FSSAI / FoSCoS: JS-rendered SPA shells, and a licence registry is a register of BUSINESSES, not product nutrition — it would not fill a panel even if reachable
tested_today.CDSCO: reachable and publishes drug data, but medicine facts have no schema home (TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS is a closed allowlist)

source_hunt_summary_2026_09_06.conclusion: Blinkit remains the only Indian source found that both permits crawling and publishes the FSS-mandated pack label as structured data, and it has been crawled to completion (90,621 of 90,628 pages). Grocery's ceiling is a property of what Indian retailers publish, not of work left undone.
source_hunt_summary_2026_09_06.what_would_change_it: A retailer or brand that publishes the mandated panel as structured page data and permits crawling. None of the ten sources above does. The remaining levers inside the repo are derivation (nova_group from ingredient lists, in progress) and the medicines schema decision, which would release roughly 30,000 facts already on disk.

financial_regulators_tested.irdai: www.irdai.gov.in — robots.txt DISALLOWS, including its own robots.txt path. So insurance's mandated disclosures cannot be taken from the regulator; the insurer's own documents (already mirrored) are the only route.
financial_regulators_tested.rbi: www.rbi.org.in — HTTP 418. An explicit refusal to non-browser clients, not a misconfiguration. Banking facts therefore come from each bank's own published schedule of charges, which is what the banking crawler already does.
financial_regulators_tested.sebi: www.sebi.gov.in — robots permits everything except /js and /css. This is already the source of the 1,283 Scheme Information Documents on disk, and it is the one open financial regulator of the three.
financial_regulators_tested.implication: Two of the three financial regulators refuse crawling, so cards, insurance and banking depend on issuer-published documents rather than a central register. That is why those domains are document-harvesting problems and funds is not.

phone_maker_spec_pages_ARE_reachable.claim_that_was_wrong: Manufacturer spec pages are JS-rendered and need browser automation. That was recorded in the plan and repeated since.
phone_maker_spec_pages_ARE_reachable.what_is_true: Five makers serve real spec content to lib/polite.py with no browser and no forged headers. Spec-token hits = occurrences of mAh, Snapdragon/Dimensity/Exynos/Tensor, and AMOLED/LCD/OLED:
phone_maker_spec_pages_ARE_reachable.robots: All five permit crawling with light restrictions — realme 2 disallows, oppo 1, mi.com 6, vivo 15, store.google.com 75. Individual paths still need checking.
phone_maker_spec_pages_ARE_reachable.what_stays_true: OnePlus's /specs pages remain a dead template (58-78 characters on every current model, zero overlap with our 16 records), and model_number is still unfillable — no maker publishes it.
phone_maker_spec_pages_ARE_reachable.scale: phones is 430 records and 24,208 slots, 0.8% of the repo, so even a perfect result moves the headline a fraction of a point. Worth doing because the domain is the weakest at 14.1% and the source is live and permitted.

cards_issuer_pages_are_live.state: 247 records at 25.9%. Twelve fields are empty on essentially every record, including cash_advance_fee and overlimit_fee (232 each), which RBI MANDATES in the Most Important Terms and Conditions.
cards_issuer_pages_are_live.why_the_MITCs_do_not_cover_it: Only 14 MITC PDFs are mirrored — one per issuer, written generically for all that issuer's cards. Card-specific fees cannot come from them.
cards_issuer_pages_are_live.the_config_is_already_sound: sources/mitc/mitc_sources.json verifies each URL individually with a %PDF magic check and explicitly warns against a blanket .bank.in rewrite, because hdfcbank.com and hdfc.bank.in both serve while sbicard.com and bobcard.co.in never moved. That is the banking lesson already applied correctly here.
cards_issuer_pages_are_live.what_is_available: sources/mitc/card_pages.json already holds per-card URLs for 15 issuers, and those pages are live. Fetched the first card page of five issuers through polite.py: SBI Card 987 KB with joining fee 42 / annual fee 263 / cash advance 3 / lounge 594 occurrences; ICICI 465 KB with joining fee 6, annual fee 7, lounge 41; Axis 692 KB with joining and annual fee 3 each. HDFC's page is 1.2 MB but names no fee at all.
cards_issuer_pages_are_live.verdict: Real, reachable, unfinished work — per-card fee pages that were discovered but never parsed. Not dispatched today only because cards is 11,115 slots, 0.4% of the repo, and five agents were already running.
cards_issuer_pages_are_live.caution: A page mentioning 'annual fee' 263 times is mostly navigation and marketing. The fee must be read from a labelled fee table, not counted in prose.

nova_group_derivation_RESULT.verdict: the derivation worked, and the refusals are the point
nova_group_derivation_RESULT.method: Implemented Open Food Facts' own published NOVA markers, validated on a held-out half of the 4,107 records that carry both an OFF-assigned group and an ingredient list. Split 50/50 by record-id hash; rules developed only against the other half.

held_out_scores.group_2: not separable from group 1 at all — REFUSED

nova_group_derivation_RESULT.overall: 97.78% accuracy where written, at 58.6% coverage, versus a crude heuristic's 81% at full coverage
nova_group_derivation_RESULT.written: 12,464 records of 26,155 carrying ingredients; 13,691 declined rather than guessed
nova_group_derivation_RESULT.distribution_check: As 1-vs-4 the result is 31.2% / 68.8% against OFF's own 27.8% / 72.2% on the labelled set — no bug signal.
nova_group_derivation_RESULT.why_groups_2_and_3_were_refused: Group 2 cannot be told from group 1 by ingredients: ghee reads as 'milk fat', mustard oil as 'mustard seeds'. Applying OFF's 2-vs-3 escalation to the declined records scores 50.8% precision, and 163 of those would be ULTRA-PROCESSED foods labelled merely 'processed' — the error that actually misleads someone reading a food registry.
audit_catches: truncated lists declaring under 100% ('Peanuts (18%)') were wrong 12 times in 16
72 combo packs with placeholder lists ('... :- NA') read as whole foods
'Contains Wheat (Gluten)' allergen notices made plain semolina ultra-processed
markers invented beyond OFF's published list (malt extract, raising agent, sugar syrup) cost precision and were removed

nova_group_remaining_gap_is_a_ceiling.state: 53,663 grocery records still have no nova_group after the derivation.
nova_group_remaining_gap_is_a_ceiling.why_not_more: NOVA needs an ingredient list, and those records do not have one. Of 24,017 food records with a Blinkit page but no stored ingredients array, a 6,000-page sample finds the page declaring an Ingredients attribute on just 113 — 1%. The parser already took essentially every declared list.
nova_group_remaining_gap_is_a_ceiling.consistent_with: the earlier corpus finding that only 20.1% of Blinkit pages carry a real ingredient DECLARATION, as distinct from marketing copy.
nova_group_remaining_gap_is_a_ceiling.the_7698_with_a_gtin: 7,698 of the 53,663 carry a GTIN, so Open Food Facts' own computed NOVA could in principle be looked up. Not pursued: the OFF dump is already established as exhausted for our records — every barcode we hold already matched a dump row and gave what it had.
nova_group_remaining_gap_is_a_ceiling.verdict: the remaining NOVA gap is an absent-input ceiling, not unfinished parsing

beauty_brandstore_RESULT.verdict: The brand-storefront route is a much smaller lever than the 16,855 low-fill records suggested, and the structural reason is now measured.
beauty_brandstore_RESULT.the_ceiling: sources/beauty/enrich_brand_specs.py already existed and gates on urls.brand matching /products/. EXACTLY 1,237 records have that, and they are already enriched — thedermaco had actives on 121 of 125 before this ran. The other 17,418 records have NO brand URL, and only ~1,600 belong to a brand with a storefront here at all. three_causes_only_one_of_which_is_a_bug.less_than_declarations_413: The dominant pattern is an escaped '<' — '<0.1 g' trans fat, '<1 mg' cholesterol. These fields are plain `number` types and cannot express a bound. Recording '<0.1' as 0.1 overstates and as 0 understates. Correctly refused; fixing it would need a schema change, not a parser change.
three_causes_only_one_of_which_is_a_bug.bare_numbers_300: Sodium's rejects are mostly a bare '3' or '25' with no unit. The parser refuses these BY DESIGN, and its comment says why: sodium is written both '4.6 mg' and '680 mg', so a bare figure could be mg or g — a thousandfold difference. Guessing is how a nutrition table ends up three orders of magnitude wrong.
three_causes_only_one_of_which_is_a_bug.well_formed_but_impossible_102: '79 g' of cholesterol per 100 g, '600 g' of calcium in 100 g. These parse cleanly, convert to 79,000 mg and 600,000 mg, and are dropped as out of range — correctly. They are retailer unit errors where mg was typed as g. The schema max for cholesterol is 5,000 mg.

why_MORE_RECORDS_cannot_reach_80_either.the_question: Every ceiling argument so far assumed the record count is fixed. It is not — Blinkit's live sitemaps project ~165,000 products against our 90,628 inventory. So: could crawling more products reach 80%?
why_MORE_RECORDS_cannot_reach_80_either.the_arithmetic: A Blinkit grocery record averages 34.6 declared slots and 15.2 filled = 43.9%. Fill is an AVERAGE over slots, and each new record brings its own empty slots.
why_MORE_RECORDS_cannot_reach_80_either.the_conclusion: Adding records that fill at 43.9% cannot raise a 43.4% average — it converges toward 43.9% and never approaches 80%. More crawling makes the catalogue LARGER and leaves the percentage where it is. This is why 'identify sources and start filling' cannot reach the target: the target is a ratio, and the source's own ceiling is the ratio's limit.
why_MORE_RECORDS_cannot_reach_80_either.what_this_completes: Four independent proofs now agree. (1) Perfect nutrition AND ingredients across all of grocery reaches 73.6%. (2) All of grocery at 100% reaches 87.69%, so 80% needs grocery near 90% against a measured ~45% source ceiling. (3) The join that would lift Blinkit records to the 63% cohort needs a barcode that exists on neither side. (4) More records converge to 43.9%. The only remaining path is the trim, which reaches 80.2% by deleting 655,493 recorded facts.
